chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father (peace be upon him) that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:
"The missed Takbirat of the funeral prayers are not made up."

The meaning in this narration is that they are not made up in the manner in which they were originally begun, with a pause between them for supplication; rather, they are made up consecutively, as al-Halabi detailed in his preceding narration.
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "And there is no objection to praying over the grave for a day and a night; if it exceeds a day and a night, the prayer is not valid."

key_terms.الْفَصْلِ: The pause or separation (between the Takbirs)
key_terms.تَكْبِيرِ الْجَنَائِزِ: The Takbirs (saying 'Allahu Akbar') of the funeral prayer
key_terms.يُقْضَى: To make up (a missed ritual act)

ai.seo_question: How are missed Takbirs in funeral prayers made up according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that missed Takbirs in funeral prayers are performed consecutively, omitting the specific supplications (du'a) inserted between them during the initial prayer, a nuance highlighted by the reference to Al-Halabi’s narration. He further establishes the jurisprudential boundary for praying over a grave, permitting it for up to a day and a night but deeming it invalid if extended beyond this period. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the ritual structure of the prayer and the temporal limits of intercessory supplication for the deceased.
